findings.problem: The study describes the second invocation of the Advent solemn blessing as 'firm in faith, glad in hope and active in charity' three times: in the Solemn Blessing locus, in 'The solemn blessing' under Each Text in Its Setting, and in the third interpretation's moral sense. The approved English of that invocation reads 'firm in faith, joyful in hope and active in charity'. SYN-006 found that wording in a secondary transcription of the 2010 ICEL Missal, and it agrees with my own knowledge of the text. The study's clause changes one word, so a reader can reconstruct the protected clause from it. The postconciliar profile allows a prayer or blessing only its Latin incipit and a description of what it asks. It forbids a paraphrase of the ICEL text close enough to reconstruct it. At line 158 the clause is followed by 'No English is printed', and the Scope appendix says the descriptions 'are not translations'. SYN-006 judged the same clause advisory in the concise study, and the synthesis review observed that the expansive study carries it three times. This is the same defect in the canonical reader. The extent is one clause. A reader is not misled about what the blessing asks. The map table already describes the invocation acceptably ('strengthen them in faith, hope and charity').
findings.required_result: Describe the invocation in words that are neither the ICEL clause nor a fresh translation of the Latin, as the map table does. For example: at 05 line 296, 'the second, that he strengthen them in faith, hope and charity in this present life;'. At 10 line 222, 'that they be strengthened in faith, hope and charity;'. At 40 line 202, 'and the solemn blessing asks him to strengthen them in faith, hope and charity.' Change nothing else in those sentences.

observations.note: STU-028, a standing advisory, reads worse in the web reader. The Douay-Rheims notice is small type in print but a full body paragraph here, so 'those words' at line 23 stands two full paragraphs after its referent, Descendisti, and directly after the notice's own words.

The Scope appendix points to instance/manifest.md, research/context.md, propers/verified.md, research/scope.md and research/interpretations.md, as the profile asks, but on the site they are unlinked code spans that a reader cannot open. The same form is in about 50 Claude proper leaves. It is a converter or site capability (linking leaf-relative record paths), not a defect of this leaf.

The generated evidence notes print article titles as ’David, King,’ and ’Chronology of the Life of Jesus Christ,’ with a right quote at each end. The corpus's straight apostrophes render that way, and TeX sets them the same in print. This belongs to the chronology corpus or generator, not to this leaf or the conversion.

limitations: Source identity does not establish semantic or rendered review acceptance.
Evidence identity covers audit/binding metadata and controlling source-record ancestry, not external witness payload verification.

summary: Artifact: the canonical study's web conversion build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s01-first-sunday-of-advent-year-b.md, conversion hash bb1020b4fb2d3c51db90c8fef7838465b3c7f967f8d44542a30f279e2f8beed0, the hash research/web-artifact.json records and REVIEW_INPUTS seals. Checked: a fresh conversion of the leaf to scratch with tools/web-edition (all fidelity audits ran) is byte-identical. Read the whole Markdown against main.tex and its ten source components (00, 05, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, the generated Scriptural Date and Location with its table, 85, 90). An in-order word comparison found no dropped or added prose. The only differences are environment titles (witness captions, lane titles), the generated chronology cells, table headers and the starred References heading. Rendered with the site's pinned Markdown renderer, reader-markup expansion and table helpers: 66 element ids, all unique; all 12 proper-* appointed-text anchors; 11 contents links, every one resolving; H1, then H2 for each section, interpretation and appendix, then H3. There are 7 blockquotes, one for each of the 7 Douay-Rheims witnesses, with the bracketed unread words kept; three four-senses definition lists with 12 terms; and 4 tables (map, comparison, chronology, branches) with every cell. No TeX debris: the 8 backslashes are all escaped brackets. The page names no model, run, workflow or release state, and the generation metadata is withheld as guidance/web-editions.md requires. The revision stamp 2026-11-26T23:01:57Z and the rights colophon are present. Both external links answer 200. The USCCB server returns a bot-check page, so its content was not confirmed. Quotations spot-checked against retained texts all match: Augustine, Enarrationes 24.2, 79.1-3, 79.9, 79.11, 84.9 in the Latin and the NPNF, and 84.15/section 12; Bede on Mark 13:34-37; Gregory, Homily 13.3, 13.5 and 13.6. Presentation: headless Chromium of that rendered article inside the site layout template, with site.css and publication-reader.css, at 1280 and 390 px. Wide tables scroll inside their own frame, as the stylesheet intends. Limits: the publication-reader shell (toolbar, contents panel, Generate PDF) could not be built, because the sealed browser products refuse with 'inputs changed' (expected mid-run), so it was not exercised. This is not a review of the deployed site. WEB-001's ICEL wording rests on SYN-006's secondary transcription, which agrees with my own knowledge of the text; the printed altar book was not read. Verdict: PASS. The conversion is faithful and complete. One advisory (a near-ICEL clause repeated in the study source) and three observations.
